Maine has three known data center facilities and a recorded total capacity of zero megawatts, making it one of the thinnest data center footprints in the northeastern United States by any power-based measure.

Two of the three facilities, both operated by FirstLight, sit in Portland and Brunswick. The third is located in Aroostook County in northern Maine and carries no operator name, no website, and no capacity figure. All three share the same problem the aggregate does: no megawatt data is available, so nothing here can be said about power draw, available capacity, or ability to support compute workloads of any scale.

What the data does establish is geographic distribution across a state that is remote from major fiber and power infrastructure relative to southern New England. Whether that remoteness constrains expansion, or whether Maine's cooler climate and available land could attract future build-out, cannot be answered by this data. The three facilities represent a presence, not a cluster, and the absence of capacity figures means the grid question, which is the binding question for AI infrastructure, remains entirely open here.
